newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's Hrawi resumes consultations on premier.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's Hrawi resumes consultations on premier.

text.p: Lebanese President Elias Hrawi resumed consultations with parliamentary deputies on Thursday to choose a new prime minister, expected to be named within hours.
Caretaker Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri seemed headed for a third term of office as 74 out of 87 MPs or representatives who met Hrawi on Wednesday backed the reappointment of the billionaire tycoon.

Hrawi, who is bound constitutionally to nominate the choice of the majority of MPs, began consulting the remainder of the 128 MPs or the heads of their parliamentary blocs on Thursday morning and is due to finish by one p.m. (1100 GMT).
Political sources have said Hrawi would name the new prime minister on Thursday, before French President Jacques Chirac arrives in Beirut on a Middle East tour.
The new prime minister would pick the government, which needs a vote of confidence from parliament, by the start of November at the latest, the sources said.

Hariri, a 51-year-old construction billionaire, has set Lebanon on the road to recovery from the 1975-90 civil war with a multi-billion dollar reconstruction programme since taking office four years ago.

The Sunni Moslem politician has headed two cabinets since October 1992. His government resigned last week to make way for a new cabinet to be formed in the wake of recent parliamentary elections but stayed on in caretaker capacity.
